newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish settler kills Palestinian man in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Jewish settler kills Palestinian man in Hebron.

text.p: A Jewish settler shot dead a Palestinian in the West Bank town of Hebron on Tuesday, raising tensions further while the United States struggles to rescue Middle East peace.

"Two Jewish seminary students were on their way to the Tomb of the Patriarchs when, according to their testimony, they were attacked by an Arab who sprayed teargas on them," West Bank police chief Yossi Sitbon said.
"Fearing for their lives, they were forced to shoot and as a result hit one of the Arabs, who Palestinians said died in hospital," he told Israel Radio.

Palestinian witnesses said a settler approached an Arab shopowner near the al-Ibrahimi mosque in an area of the city still under Israeli control and shot him. They said the Palestinian died instantly.
Israeli police said the settler was detained.
"We have a martyr. His name is Asem Rashad Kamel Arafah, 24 years, and he was shot in the chest. They told us he was shot by a settler," an official at Hebron hospital told Reuters.
After the shooting, clashes erupted along the tense confrontation line dividing the Israeli- and Palestinian-controlled parts of Hebron.
Palestinians threw petrols bombs at Israeli soldiers who responded with rubber bullets. Hospital officials said 16 Palestinians were injured.
A Palestinian witness saw a soldier jump on a settler who opened fire towards demonstrators and take him away.

Daily clashes have erupted in the West Bank since Israel broke ground for a Jewish housing project in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18 which Palestinians charged will complete a ring of Israeli settlements on disputed land around the city.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu left Washington to return to Israel late on Monday after a tough two-hour meeting with President Bill Clinton failed to revive the Israeli-Palestinian peace talks.

The White House said Clinton offered new ideas to end an escalating spiral of violence but no progress was reported after a session that the president described as "very specific, frank, candid and long".
Jibril Rajoub, head of Palestinian Preventive Security in the West Bank, called the Hebron incident "very dangerous" and demanded protection for Palestinians in the Israeli-held side of the city.

"This is an immediate result of the (settlement) policies of Mr Netanyahu. I hope he will be happy seeing this blood on his own hands," Marwan Kanafani, a spokesman for Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said in Gaza.
Some 400 settlers live in Israeli-controlled enclaves in Hebron, home to more than 100,000 Arabs.

On Monday, a Jewish settler shot and seriously wounded a Palestinian in the village of Kharbatha, 17 kms (10 miles) west of the PLO-controlled town of Ramallah. The settler was detained for questioning.
About 130,000 Jewish settlers, most of whom are armed by the military, live in heavily fortified enclaves in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
